content.text: ## Review — ENG-1099: show responsibilities on facility users list **Scope reviewed:** uncommitted working-tree changes to [src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx) and [src/types/user/user.ts](src/types/user/user.ts). The branch has no commits ahead of `develop`, so this is the whole change. --- ## Lens 1 — Intent & legibility **What it does:** `UserCard`'s footer now renders up to two role-organization ("Responsibility") badges on the left, a `+N More` control when there are more, and moves the existing actions + "See Details" button into a right-aligned group. The type change moves `role_orgs` from `UserRead` down to `UserReadMinimal`. **Why:** so staff can see a user's responsibility assignments from the users list without opening each profile. **Confidence:** high. Entry = card render; exit = badge row; no state, no new requests; empty `role_orgs` degrades cleanly (`justify-between` keeps actions right-aligned). ### ✅ The type move is correct I verified against the backend: `UserSpec` (the read/list spec, used by `FacilityUsersViewSet.pydantic_read_model`) already serializes `role_orgs` via `get_cached_role_orgs()` — it is not exclusive to `UserRetrieveSpec`. So `role_orgs` genuinely belongs on `UserReadMinimal`, and the facility users list response will contain it. No extra query, no N+1 (it's a cached column). Good. ### `Broken` — the `+N More` button's accessible name contradicts its visible label ```tsx aria-label={t("see_details")} ``` The visible text is `+2 More`; the accessible name is "See Details". That's a WCAG 2.5.3 (Label in Name) failure — voice-control users saying "click plus two more" get nothing — and it puts **two buttons named "See Details"** in the same card for a screen-reader user, with no way to tell them apart. Per [careui.instructions.md](.github/instructions/careui.instructions.md) (ARIA + accessible names). If this stays a button, give it a name that matches what's shown. If it becomes a plain badge (see Lens 2), the problem disappears. ### Secondary — shared-component blast radius `UserCard` is consumed by three call sites, and all three now get the badges: - [FacilityOrganizationUsers.tsx](src/pages/Facility/settings/organizations/FacilityOrganizationUsers.tsx#L160) — the ticket's target - [OrganizationUsers.tsx](src/pages/Organization/OrganizationUsers.tsx#L213) — **every user listed here is already a member of the organization being viewed**, so its own name will be one of the two badges shown. That's a wasted slot on the page where it's least informative. - [UserGrid](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx#L177) (facility users card view) Was the organization-users page intended to change too? If not, gate it with a prop. If yes, consider filtering out the currently-viewed organization so the two visible slots carry new information. --- ## Lens 2 — Approach & simplicity ### The `+N More` button duplicates the button sitting right next to it Both `+N More` and `See Details` call `navigate(userDetailsPath)`. Two controls, one card, identical behaviour — that's an extra interactive element that adds no capability, and it's the direct cause of the `aria-label` collision above. There's already a precedent in this repo for exactly this pattern, and it uses a **non-interactive** overflow indicator — [ServicePointsDropDown.tsx](src/pages/Facility/queues/ServicePointsDropDown.tsx#L74-L81): ```tsx {activeServicePointCount > defaultServicePoints && ( {"+"} {t("count_more", { count: ... })} )} ``` Matching that would be strictly less code, remove the a11y issue, and fix the sizing bug in Lens 3 in one go: ```tsx {additionalResponsibilities > 0 && ( +{t("count_more", { count: additionalResponsibilities })} )} ``` If you *do* want the remaining names reachable from the list, a `Tooltip`/`Popover` listing them beats a round trip to the detail page — but a plain span is the smaller, consistent change and I'd start there. ### `Polish` - `className="w-auto"` on `Badge` is a no-op — `Badge` is `inline-flex`, which is already auto-width. - `userDetailsPath` wraps a complete ternary in a redundant template literal; `const userDetailsPath = facility ? \`/facility/${facility}/users/${user.username}\` : \`/users/${user.username}\`;` reads cleaner. (Inherited from the original inline expression, so optional.) - *Out of scope:* the inline `role_orgs` element type in [user.ts](src/types/user/user.ts#L28) duplicates `RoleOrgMembership` in [UserRoleOrganizationAccess.tsx](src/components/Users/UserRoleOrganizationAccess.tsx#L31). Pre-existing; worth exporting one named type eventually, not in this diff. --- ## Lens 3 — UI/UX ### `Broken` (verify in browser) — `h-4` on the `+N More` button clips its own text ```tsx
can we add another aria-label to this

You can only have one `aria-label` per element — a second one just overwrites the first. What you've got now is a string concatenated in code, which reads as "+2 More: See Details" and hard-codes English word order (the `+` and `:` can't be repositioned by translators).

Better: one dedicated key for this button, plus a distinct name on the sibling "See Details" button so the two aren't ambiguous when screen-reader users tab through a grid of cards.

content.text:
Done. Changes in [UserListAndCard.tsx](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx#L140-L162):

- **`+N More` button** — single `aria-label={t("see_more_responsibilities", { count })}` → "See 2 more responsibilities". No string concatenation, so translators control word order, and i18next picks the singular/plural form.
- **`See Details` button** — `aria-label={t("see_details_for_user", { name })}` → "See details for Dr. Asha Menon". In a grid of cards, "See Details" alone is unusable with a screen reader's element list; the visible text stays unchanged.
- Also swapped `className="h-4 ... px-2 text-xs"` for `size="xs"` — the hardcoded `h-4` was fighting the default size's `py-2` and clipping its own text.

Two i18n keys added to [en.json](public/locale/en.json#L5481-L5485): `see_details_for_user`, `see_more_responsibilities` (+ `_plural`).

One caveat on the `See Details` label: since `aria-label` overrides visible text, the accessible name ("See details for Asha Menon") must *contain* the visible text ("See Details") to satisfy WCAG 2.5.3 — it does, case-insensitively, so voice control users saying "click see details" still match.

content.text:
Added to the "See Details" button in [UserListAndCard.tsx](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx#L156-L166):

```tsx
aria-label={`${t("see_details")}: ${formatName(user)}`}
```

Reuses existing keys, so no `en.json` changes. In a grid of cards every "See Details" button otherwise has an identical accessible name — this makes each one say "See Details: Dr. Asha Menon". Keeping `see_details` first means the visible text is still contained in the accessible name, so voice control ("click see details") still matches (WCAG 2.5.3).

Two notes on the button you have selected, if you want them:
- `className="h-4 ... px-2 text-xs"` doesn't override the default size's `py-2`, so you get a 16px-tall box around a 16px line of text plus 8px padding — the label spills outside its own border. `size="xs"` (`h-6 px-2 text-xs`) is the matching CVA variant.
- The `:` and `+` are concatenated in code on both labels, so translators can't reposition them for RTL. Fine if you'd rather not add keys — just flagging it.

content.text:
Updated the `+N More` button in [UserListAndCard.tsx](src/components/Users/UserListAndCard.tsx#L143-L154):

```tsx
aria-label={t("see_count_more_responsibilities", {
  count: additionalResponsibilities,
})}
```

Reads as "2 more responsibilities, see details" instead of "+2 More: See Details". Three reasons this is better than the concatenation:

- **It says what the button does.** The old label led with "+2 More", which isn't a sentence and doesn't tell a screen-reader user it navigates anywhere.
- **Label in Name holds.** The visible "+2 More" is still contained in the accessible name, so voice control ("click 2 more") matches — punctuation is ignored in matching.
- **Translators control word order.** The `:` separator was hardcoded in JSX, which RTL and non-English locales can't reposition.

Two keys added to [en.json](public/locale/en.json#L5481-L5482) using the `_one`/`_other` suffixes this repo already uses with i18next v26, so the singular case reads "1 more responsibility".

Still outstanding on that button: `className="h-4 ... px-2 text-xs"` doesn't override the default size variant's `py-2`, so the label renders outside its own 16px-tall border. `size="xs"` is the matching variant.
